lessons.trace: The stop callback runs before the wait callback. Real callbacks would signal a worker and then join or await it.
lessons.caution: Callbacks must not throw or re-enter evaluation. In C++, explicitly close before captured locals are destroyed if destruction order would otherwise leave dangling captures.
lessons.exercise: Register two resources and record that both stop events precede either wait event.

lessons.title: Idempotent close
lessons.concept: close is guarded against repeated shutdown. This lets an application call it at an explicit lifecycle boundary even though the C++ destructor also invokes it. Keep teardown logic in the callbacks idempotent where practical.
lessons.trace: The first call drains the registered resource list. The second observes the closing state and returns.
lessons.caution: Idempotent resource shutdown does not imply the session can be reopened. Construct a new session for a new lifecycle.
lessons.exercise: Attempt resource registration after close and handle the resulting rejection.

lessons.title: Limiting evaluation depth
lessons.concept: set_max_depth bounds interpreter recursion and evaluation depth according to the implementation checks. It is a useful guard while developing recursive scripts, but cannot stop an arbitrary blocking native callback.
lessons.trace: A shallow expression remains valid under the configured depth. More deeply nested evaluation can fail with a language diagnostic.
lessons.caution: Depth is not wall-clock time, total allocation or instruction count. Use a separate process and explicit resource budgets when stronger containment is required.
lessons.exercise: Create a terminating recursive function and measure the depth at which it starts failing.

title: Deployment and cross-dialect verification
aim: Make paths, dependencies and evidence explicit before distributing an embedding.
architecture: The four source files are pinned in vendor. MetaML standard-library discovery checks environment, installation-relative and fallback paths. Import resolution and callback capabilities should be tested under the same deployment layout users will receive.

lessons.title: Explicit standard-library discovery
lessons.concept: load_stdlib searches for prelude/mod.ml and returns a Result. A missing installation is an actionable configuration failure. The book does not invent metalib contents or claim those modules were bundled with the supplied headers.
lessons.trace: The explicit directory disables fallback discovery for this attempt. The deliberately absent path produces a controlled failure.
lessons.caution: Do not ignore load_stdlib and then blame undefined names on the language parser. Report installation failures at startup.
lessons.exercise: Install a real metalib tree separately and repeat with an explicit absolute path.

lessons.title: Import search paths
lessons.concept: Add a controlled search directory before loading application modules. The session exposes search_paths for inspection, allowing a diagnostic screen to show where imports will be sought without guessing from the process working directory.
lessons.trace: The host path is now part of resolution configuration. Adding a path does not itself import or execute a module.
lessons.caution: Relative paths depend on the process working directory. Convert deployment roots to intentional absolute paths when reproducibility matters.
lessons.exercise: Run from two different working directories and compare resolution behavior.

lessons.title: Unresolved imports are inspectable
lessons.concept: resolve_import answers where an import would resolve without executing it. This is useful for editor navigation and startup diagnostics. The answer is optional because resolution can legitimately fail.
lessons.trace: No matching file produces absence rather than a fabricated path. A real import attempt can then provide the appropriate language diagnostic.
lessons.caution: Resolution alone is not a guarantee that a later read succeeds; files can change between inspection and loading.
lessons.exercise: Resolve a real module and compare the canonical path with imported_files after loading it.

lessons.title: Discovering installed primitive names
lessons.concept: primitive_names exposes the host vocabulary. Use it to audit a prepared session and to compare C++ and D deployments. Discovery is distinct from authorization: an installed primitive can exist while remaining disallowed.
lessons.trace: The constructor installs core primitives before any external prelude is loaded. The audit therefore sees a nonempty vocabulary.
lessons.caution: Do not use a displayed list as an authorization check. Consult the configured capability policy at the call boundary.
lessons.exercise: Sort and compare the two dialect inventories when a D compiler becomes available.

lessons.title: Portable scripts and native adapters
lessons.concept: The most useful cross-dialect fixture runs exactly the same MetaML source under both hosts. Compare rendered values, inferred types and diagnostics, while keeping native adapter tests separate so one failure points to the correct layer.
lessons.trace: The program uses syntax and core arithmetic only, so it is independent of external filesystem layout.
lessons.caution: The supplied source comments demand dialect parity, but comments are not evidence that every path behaves identically. Run differential tests rather than assuming parity.
lessons.exercise: Add an error fixture and compare diagnostic code and span before comparing presentation text.
lessons.ml:
val square := fn x -> x * x
square 6 + 6

title: Case study I: a formula optimization tool
aim: Build a command-oriented optimizer for a deliberately small, pure expression language. The input is a first-order S-expression with integer atoms and add or mul nodes. The output is a reduced expression plus an explicit stop status.
architecture: The front end parses structure, validates arity and atom syntax, then applies a sound rule set for the chosen integer model. A destructive reducer gives a reproducible baseline; an e-graph retains alternatives. A host wrapper owns diagnostics and rejects unsupported operators before optimization.

lessons.title: Specify and validate the formula input
lessons.concept: The language contract permits nonnegative integer atoms and binary add or mul forms. The case study begins with structural recognition rather than evaluating arbitrary S-expressions. An optimizer must reject a malformed tree before a rewrite has a chance to hide the malformed part.
lessons.trace: The first checks establish the expected binary root shape. The complete tool supplied with the book validates recursively and rejects unknown operators and invalid atoms.
lessons.caution: These local assertions demonstrate one fixture; they are not the whole validator. The standalone case-study program includes the recursive boundary validation.
lessons.exercise: Reject (add 42), (unknown 1 2), a quoted numeric atom, and an atom with trailing letters.

lessons.title: Normalize with a small sound rule set
lessons.concept: Start with identity rules whose correctness is easy to explain under the chosen pure arithmetic model: adding zero and multiplying by one. Avoid distributivity until the cost model and growth budget are ready. Do not simplify effects because the input language intentionally contains none.
lessons.trace: Two local identities remove the add and mul nodes. The returned step count gives a compact regression signal.
lessons.caution: If the domain later adds checked operations or effectful operands, revisit every rule proof. A familiar algebraic identity is not automatically valid in every semantics.
lessons.exercise: Add the symmetric identities and test both child positions.

lessons.title: Compare with equality saturation
lessons.concept: Use the same identities in an e-graph so alternative forms remain available. This separates the legality argument from extraction preference. Record the report even when the extracted expression looks correct, because budget exhaustion is a performance and completeness signal.
lessons.trace: Saturation merges the nested identities into equivalence classes. Extraction finds the one-atom expression at minimum node cost.
lessons.caution: Equality saturation retains alternatives and can use more memory than a directional reducer. Choose it for a reason, not because it sounds universally more advanced.
lessons.exercise: Compare nodes, iterations and output size on a deeply nested identity expression.

lessons.title: Make budget stops observable
lessons.concept: A command-line tool must distinguish successful normalization from a partial result. A zero-step budget is a useful acceptance fixture because it exposes a pending redex without allowing any change. Return a distinct exit status for this condition.
lessons.trace: The system detects that another rewrite exists but refuses to perform it. The original term is preserved and StepLimit is returned.
lessons.caution: Do not print only the term and exit zero. That would make an incomplete optimization indistinguishable from a proven normal form.
lessons.exercise: Add a command-line budget argument and an acceptance test for exit status two.

lessons.title: Structural regression and semantic regression
lessons.concept: Compare an optimized tree with the expected shape, then separately compare arithmetic meaning under the language model. Shape tests catch rule-order regressions; semantic tests catch invalid rules. Neither category replaces the other.
lessons.trace: The reduced term is smaller while the original parsed representation remains available for reporting. The complete case tool evaluates both sides modulo an explicit unsigned width.
lessons.caution: Random testing increases confidence but does not prove all rules sound. Keep a short written argument for every rewrite and include overflow-edge fixtures.
lessons.exercise: Generate depth-bounded formulas and compare before/after evaluation for hundreds of fixed-seed inputs.

title: Case study II: a reloadable decision service
aim: Embed MetaML as a typed policy layer while retaining host control of data, capabilities and publication. A policy receives native facts through a narrow interface and returns a decision.
architecture: A candidate session is prepared separately, checked with acceptance fixtures and published only after validation. Evaluation failure produces an application error rather than an implicit allow. Existing sessions remain alive until in-flight work completes. The standalone C++ and D programs demonstrate candidate validation without requiring an external standard library.

lessons.title: A pure policy contract
lessons.concept: The initial policy maps an integer fact to a Boolean decision. Pure logic is easy to test before host callbacks are added. Put the policy contract in one module so callers do not depend on its internal helper names.
lessons.trace: The module exports one function. Its comparison returns a Boolean that the host can validate before using it as an authorization decision.
lessons.caution: An evaluation error is different from a false policy result. Keep a three-way host outcome: allow, deny, or policy failure.
lessons.exercise: Test ages seventeen, eighteen and nineteen. Keep the exact boundary in the policy acceptance contract.

lessons.title: Supplying facts through typed callbacks
lessons.concept: The host supplies trusted request facts through a narrow primitive. The script decides how to combine those facts. This avoids interpolating untrusted request data into executable source and gives the capability review a small vocabulary to inspect.
lessons.trace: The request fact crosses as an integer through the typed adapter. No source quoting is required.
lessons.caution: Do not mutate a captured request object while another thread evaluates the session. This example is deliberately confined to one evaluation thread.
lessons.exercise: Supply a Boolean verified fact as a separate callback and require both checks.

lessons.title: Validating a reload candidate
lessons.concept: A candidate session should pass both type checks and behavioral fixtures before publication. Keeping it separate prevents a failed reload from poisoning the currently active environment. The complete case program uses independent ownership for active and candidate sessions.
lessons.trace: The result type is checked independently from the denial fixture. A function returning an Int is rejected before it can become the active decision policy.
lessons.caution: A few fixtures cannot establish every business rule. They are a publication gate backed by a documented contract, not a proof of policy correctness.
lessons.exercise: Prepare a candidate that always allows and verify the denial fixture rejects it.

lessons.title: Denying ambient native access
lessons.concept: After registering intended facts, replace the allowlist with the exact names the policy needs. The explicit policy should be reviewed after every native extension is added. Avoid enabling all primitives as a shortcut during production startup.
lessons.trace: The requested fact is permitted and the comparison succeeds. Unrelated non-core names are outside the configured list.
lessons.caution: Core primitives remain allowed and native callbacks can do whatever their host implementation permits. Use process isolation when policy code requires a stronger trust boundary.
lessons.exercise: Register an unrelated primitive, then demonstrate that this final allowlist denies it.

lessons.title: Failure reporting and publication discipline
lessons.concept: A malformed candidate should be discarded with useful diagnostics while the active policy remains available. The publication step exchanges an owned session reference only after validation. In a concurrent service, serialize each session use or allocate separate evaluators with a documented synchronization model.
lessons.trace: The invalid candidate is a different session, so its failure cannot replace active bindings. The active policy still evaluates successfully.
lessons.caution: Swapping a pointer is not the entire concurrency design. In-flight readers need ownership of the old session, and shutdown must wait until their resources are no longer in use.
lessons.exercise: Extend the standalone case program with a publication generation number and retain the previous generation on validation failure.
